userStories.title: Classify and boundedly re-run starved checks in the CI wait
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] waitForChecks on GitHub reads checks with ["gh", "pr", "checks", <prRef>, "--json", "name,state,bucket,link"].

routing.reasoning: Stateful bounded reruns, stale GitHub job identity, SHA binding, deadline/error priorities and progress logging must integrate without changing one-shot reads or increasing loop complexity.

suggestedCriteria: After a rerun, a poll still reporting that cancelled job id issues neither another job read nor another POST.

userStories.title: Keep starved publish results as drafts without agent repair
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve and explain runner starvation in workflow publish records while opting publish into reruns and excluding it from CI agent repair.

**Motivation** — A starved check is not a failure to repair.

**Approach** — Add `"starved"` to `FeatureCiState`, make `ciReason` return the prefixed detail for it, add it to `DETAILED_CI_STATES`, and pass `rerunStarved: true` from the publish's `waitForCi`.

`ciReason` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/approval.ts`): target also returns `CI starved: <detail>` for `"starved"` with a detail, and `CI checks never got a runner` without one.

`DETAILED_CI_STATES` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts`): target also holds `"starved"`, so the published record keeps the wait's detail.

The re-run is opt-in per caller. The run's publish (`waitForCi` in `packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts`) and `nax bot fix` (`waitForCi` in `packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts`) pass `rerunStarved: true`. `nax workflow promote` does not: it is a one-poll check and, without `--yes`, a report that must not write to the forge. This story changes only publish's caller.

`ciRepairPlan` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-repair-steps.ts`) — plans a repair only for `out.ci === "failed"`. Keep that guard unchanged; exercise it with a starved draft to prove no CI read or repair is planned. The strict-green rule (ruled 2026-10-21) stands: `pending`, `unavailable` and the new `starved` still block. What changes is that "never ran" is named, re-run, and can be accepted on the record.

Update the existing assertion in `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/finalize-ci.test.ts` at lines 77-79: its pinned options object gains `rerunStarved: true` and is otherwise unchanged. New optional fields are spread in only when set, so payloads without them are exactly today's. Test publish through `_featureDeps.waitForChecks`, including returned draft outcome, CI state, retained detail and readiness reason.

**Scope** — In: feature CI union, starved reason/fallback, detail retention, publish rerun opt-in and no-repair regression. Out: wait implementation (US-002), optional readiness exception (US-004), waiver comments/commands/status (US-005/006/007/008). The run's own publish never waives: a starved CI keeps the draft until a human runs `nax bot fix --waive-starved` or `nax workflow promote --waive-starved`.

**Interface** —
```ts
export type FeatureCiState = "green" | "failed" | "pending" | "skipped" | "conflicting" | "no-checks" | "unavailable" | "starved";
export function ciReason(ci: FeatureCiState | undefined, detail?: string): string | undefined;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] ciReason("starved", "1 check(s) never got a runner: x; re-run them, or accept with --waive-starved <reason>") returns "CI starved: 1 check(s) never got a runner: x; re-run them, or accept with --waive-starved <reason>".
[unit] ciReason("starved") returns "CI checks never got a runner".
[unit] readinessReasons with ci: starved and a detail returns a list that holds ciReason("starved", <that detail>).

[integration] publish calls the stubbed _featureDeps.waitForChecks with options that include rerunStarved: true, preserving the existing cwd, timeoutMs, pollMs, signal and expectedSha values unchanged.
[integration] When the stubbed _featureDeps.waitForChecks returns outcome starved with detail d, publish returns outcome draft, ci starved and ciDetail d.
[unit] Regression guard: ciRepairPlan for a draft publish outcome whose ci is starved returns undefined and runs no CI read.

routing.reasoning: Additive state propagation across existing publish/reason helpers; the repair exclusion already exists and needs a behavioral regression guard.

userStories.title: Allow an explicit starved-only CI readiness waiver
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the shared CI readiness rule with an explicit starved-only exception and thread it through workflowPrReadiness.

**Motivation** — Nothing can release the PR.

**Approach** — The waiver is one rule extension and one record. `ciAllowsReady(outcome, { waiveStarved: true })` also allows `starved`; it never allows `failed`, `pending`, `conflicting`, `no-checks` or `unavailable`.

Add the `waiveStarved` option to `ciAllowsReady` and to `workflowPrReadiness`.

`workflowPrReadiness` input (`packages/nax/src/bot/workflow-ready.ts`) — Baseline: `{ outcome?; ci: CiWaitResult; coverage?; headSha? }` — Target: the same plus `readonly waiveStarved?: boolean`, passed through to `ciAllowsReady`.

Without `waiveStarved` both functions behave as today; the existing tests pin that. Keep all workflow item, index, confirmed-work and coverage checks ahead of the shared CI decision; the option only changes which CI outcomes pass, never another readiness condition. New optional fields are spread in only when set, so payloads without them are exactly today's.

**Scope** — In: shared predicate and workflow readiness option, with a matrix proving true only for green or explicitly waived starved. Out: reason validation and durable records (US-005), waiver posting, CLI flags and ready commands (US-007/008), publish state propagation (US-003), live status (US-006). The run's own publish never waives: a starved CI keeps the draft until a human runs `nax bot fix --waive-starved` or `nax workflow promote --waive-starved`.

**Interface** —
```ts
ciAllowsReady(outcome: CiWaitOutcome, options?: { readonly waiveStarved?: boolean }): boolean
```
`workflowPrReadiness` retains its existing return union and existing input fields; add `readonly waiveStarved?: boolean` to its input object.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] ciAllowsReady("starved") returns false.
[unit] ciAllowsReady("starved", { waiveStarved: true }) returns true.
[unit] ciAllowsReady("green", { waiveStarved: true }) returns true.
[unit] ciAllowsReady with { waiveStarved: true } returns false for each outcome in ["failed", "pending", "conflicting", "no-checks", "unavailable"].
[unit] workflowPrReadiness with every item settled, ci outcome starved and waiveStarved: true returns { ready: true }.
[unit] workflowPrReadiness with every item settled and ci outcome starved without waiveStarved returns { ready: false } whose reason starts with "CI starved:".

[unit] Without a waiveStarved option, ciAllowsReady returns true for green and false for each existing non-green outcome failed, pending, conflicting, no-checks and unavailable, preserving the existing strict-green rule.

routing.reasoning: Small optional policy extension in two existing helpers; no authentication, role, permission or credential mechanism changes.

suggestedCriteria: workflowPrReadiness still returns ready:false for an open workflow item when waiveStarved:true and CI is starved.
workflowPrReadiness still returns ready:false for uncovered required files at the current head when waiveStarved:true and CI is starved.
ciAllowsReady("starved", { waiveStarved: false }) returns false.

userStories.title: Report durable CI waivers in live workflow status
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose a ready PR's durable CI waiver in live workflow status JSON and plain output.

**Motivation** — The only escape was `gh pr ready` by hand, which leaves `nax workflow status` at `outcome: draft` and no record of why a merged PR carries a check that never ran.

**Approach** — `readLiveStatus` reads `latestCiWaiver` from the comments it already lists; `nax workflow status` puts it in `--json` as `ciWaiver` and prints the waiver line, only when the live PR is not a draft.

`LiveStatus` live arm (`packages/nax/src/workflow/live-status.ts`): target adds `readonly ciWaiver?: CiWaiver`.

`WorkflowStatusReport` (`packages/nax/src/cli/workflow.ts`): target adds `readonly ciWaiver?: CiWaiver`; `printPlain` adds the waiver line.

`nax workflow status`: when the live read finds a waiver and the PR is no longer a draft, `--json` carries `ciWaiver: { headSha, checks, reason }` and the plain output adds `CI: passed with waiver at <sha7>: <n> check(s) never got a runner (<a>; <b>): <reason>`.

New optional fields (`starvedChecks`, `rerunStarved`, `waiveStarved`, `ciWaiver`, `ciWaived`) are spread in only when set, so payloads without them are exactly today's. Reuse the current login and comment list fetched alongside PR state; preserve no-item-index fallback, existing live-read eligibility and unrelated open-item reporting. Filter ciWaiver out of the public report when the PR remains a draft; do not rewrite the historical record or fabricate green CI. Place the plain waiver line before the supplementary-items early return. Exercise readLiveStatus and workflowStatusCommand, not only render helpers.

**Scope** — In: live waiver read, optional report field, ready-PR plain line and absence regressions. Out: record grammar (US-005), posting/waiving/readiness commands (US-007/008), polling outcomes (US-002). `nax workflow status` shows a waiver only on a live read; a status that falls back to the run record (for example a PR with no item index) does not show it. `latestCiWaiver` reads only comments by the current forge login, as the item index does; a waiver posted by another account is not shown.

**Interface** — Add `readonly ciWaiver?: CiWaiver` to both the live arm of `LiveStatus` and `WorkflowStatusReport`; `CiWaiver` is the interface exported by US-005. Existing command signatures and fallback arm stay unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] readLiveStatus over a PR whose comments hold the item index and an own w-ci-waiver comment returns a live status whose ciWaiver equals that comment parsed by parseCiWaiver.
[integration] workflowStatusCommand with json: true for a ready PR carrying an own waiver prints a report whose ciWaiver holds the waiver's headSha, checks and reason.
[integration] The plain workflowStatusCommand output for the same PR includes "CI: passed with waiver at <sha7>: 1 check(s) never got a runner (<name>): <reason>".
[integration] workflowStatusCommand with json: true for a PR with no waiver comment prints a report with no ciWaiver key.
[integration] workflowStatusCommand with json: true for a PR that is still a draft and carries an own waiver prints a report with no ciWaiver key.

userStories.title: Waive starved CI safely through nax bot fix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add validated --waive-starved support to full and ready-only bot fix passes, recording the waiver before readiness and reporting it.

**Motivation** — Nothing can release the PR.

**Approach** — Add the CLI option, validate it, and thread the reason through `BotFixInput` into `BotFixEnv`. The ready pass's CI wait re-runs starved jobs. A `starved` outcome with a reason posts the waiver comment and then marks the PR ready, on both the workflow-PR path and the plain-PR path; `workflowReadyHold` returns the waiver it recorded, and `ready.produces` declares `ciWaived`. The decision and the comment write live in `packages/nax/src/bot/ci-waiver-ready.ts`. The fix summary comment and the command's summary line name the waiver.

`nax bot fix <pr> --waive-starved <reason>`: also accepted with `--ready-only`. The reason is validated by `parseWaiverReason` before any fix or forge call; an invalid reason prints the error on stderr and exits 1. When the ready pass's CI wait ends `starved`, the pass posts the waiver comment, then marks the PR ready. On the full fix path (not `--ready-only`, which posts no fix summary) the fix summary comment adds `Marked ready with a CI waiver: <n> check(s) never got a runner: <a>; <b>. Reason: <reason>`, and the command's own summary line reads `Marked ready with a CI waiver: <n> check(s) never got a runner.` When CI is green the flag changes nothing. When any check really failed the pass keeps the draft as today.

On the workflow path the waiver comment is posted after `writeEvidence` and before the final PR head re-read; on the plain path after `readyHeadHold`; on both, before the mark-ready command. `ci-waiver-ready.ts` catches its own post error and returns it as the `could not record the CI waiver: <error>` hold, so the catch in `workflowReadyHold` never sees it. The file is 556 lines against the 600-line limit, so the waiver decision and its comment write live in the new `packages/nax/src/bot/ci-waiver-ready.ts`, and `fix-report.ts` only calls it.

A caller that readies a PR under a waiver first posts a `w-ci-waiver` comment (`renderCiWaiver`) and marks the PR ready only when that post succeeded. Use the exact execution head (`state.pushedSha ?? env.info.headSha`) and the CI result's starvedChecks for the record; pass the already-validated reason and do not waive any other CI outcome. `ciAllowsReady(outcome, { waiveStarved: true })` also allows `starved`; it never allows `failed`, `pending`, `conflicting`, `no-checks` or `unavailable`. `workflowPrReadiness` receives the optional waiveStarved flag, preserving item and coverage conditions. `waitForCi` in fix-report.ts passes `rerunStarved: true`. Preserve the existing review/findings/head-gate/head-race/cancellation checks and the _fixReportDeps seams; inject the comment writer into the new helper so outer readyStep tests still observe it.

`BotFixOptions` (`packages/nax/src/cli/bot.ts`), `BotFixInput` (`packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts`), `BotFixEnv` (`packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts`): target each adds `readonly waiveStarved?: string` (the validated reason). The `env` object built in `runBotFix` (`fix-run.ts`) copies it from the input. `BotFixState` (`packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts`): target adds `readonly ciWaived?: { readonly checks: readonly string[]; readonly reason: string }`. `BOT_FIX_GRAPH.ready.produces` target is `["markedReady", "readyHeld", "ciWaived"]` — `assertPatchDeclared` rejects any undeclared key. `readinessSummary` target prints `Marked ready with a CI waiver: <n> check(s) never got a runner.` when `ciWaived` is set.

New optional fields (`starvedChecks`, `rerunStarved`, `waiveStarved`, `ciWaiver`, `ciWaived`) are spread in only when set, so payloads without them are exactly today's. Treat undefined as absent, not an empty string: empty, multiline, over-300-character or <!---holding reasons must fail before orchestration. Without `--waive-starved` the ready pass is today's; the existing bot fix tests pin that path. Use botFixCommand and runBotFix as outer triggers with `_fixReportDeps.waitForChecks` stubbed, in addition to focused readyStep tests on both PR paths. readyStep's return is StepResult<BotFixState>: assert markedReady, readyHeld and ciWaived under result.patch; runBotFix's BotFixResult exposes those state fields directly. Observe the private readinessSummary through botFixCommand's emitted ready-pass line rather than exporting it solely for tests. When a fixture sets state.pushedSha, set state.readyOnly:true to reach the ready-pass checks instead of the existing pushed-head hold.

**Scope** — In: bot CLI registration/early validation, full-cycle and ready-only propagation, ready wait opt-in, extracted helper, durable comment-before-ready sequencing, graph output and reports. Out: CI classification (US-002), shared rule (US-004), record helpers (US-005), workflow promote (US-008), status (US-006). `readChecksOnce` (the one-shot read behind `nax bot fix`'s gate baseline) keeps its current outcomes; a starved check there still reads as `failed`.

**Interface** —
```ts
// BotFixOptions, BotFixInput and BotFixEnv each add:
readonly waiveStarved?: string;
// BotFixState adds:
readonly ciWaived?: { readonly checks: readonly string[]; readonly reason: string };
// workflowReadyHold target:
workflowReadyHold(env, state): Promise<{ readonly held?: string; readonly ciWaived?: BotFixState["ciWaived"] }>
```

routing.reasoning: Cross-module CLI/input/environment/state propagation and two guarded readiness paths require durable write ordering, specific failure holds and declared step-graph outputs; existing forge access checks remain unchanged.

[integration] With every item ruled, a stubbed CI wait returning starved for check x and waiveStarved: "runner starvation", the report's ci-green check has passed: true and detail "waived: x".
[integration] In the same case without yes, no forge write command runs and the plain output includes "pass  ci-green  waived: x".
[integration] In the same case with yes: true, the report's action names are tick, comment, waiver, ready, record in that order, and waiver has status done.

[integration] In the same case with yes: true, the waiver action sends the argv constructed by commentArgv for the PR through forgeDeps.forge.run, with a body that parseCiWaiver reads as { headSha: <PR head>, checks: ["x"], reason: "runner starvation" }.
[integration] When the waiver write exits 1 with stderr denied, the command returns 1 with the error "promote stopped at waiver: denied", and the mark-ready command never runs.
[integration] With yes: true, waiveStarved set and a stubbed CI wait returning green, the waiver action has status skipped and no waiver comment is posted.
[integration] With yes: true, no waiveStarved and a green CI, the report's action names are tick, comment, ready, record.
[integration] With a stubbed CI wait returning starved and no waiveStarved, the ci-green check fails with detail starting "ci starved:".
[integration] With waiveStarved set and a stubbed CI wait returning failed, the ci-green check fails with detail starting "ci failed:".

[integration] workflowPromoteCommand rejects an empty, multiline, over-300-character or <!---holding waiver reason with exit 1 and reports the parseWaiverReason validation error before any forge call (the thrown NaxError has code CI_WAIVER_REASON_INVALID).
[integration] When the waiver action fails, the promotion does not run the record action.

routing.reasoning: Two existing CLI modules gain an option and one action using the established ciGreen, forgeWrite and ordered-action patterns; injected forge fixtures make ordinary single-session TDD sufficient.

suggestedCriteria: When two starved check names include commas, the passing ci-green detail joins the complete names with semicolon-space.
When a valid reason has surrounding whitespace, the posted waiver record uses the trimmed reason.
When ci-green passes with no detail, plain output remains exactly pass  ci-green.
When a waived promotion succeeds, the posted waiver's headSha equals the exact expectedSha passed to the single CI wait.

Mirror that fail-soft I/O pattern, but do not reuse failed-step classification or add a runner_id requirement: starvation requires conclusion cancelled, runner_name empty or null, and an actual empty steps array. New ci-starved.ts owns URL recognition, job reads, POST reruns, CI_STARVED_RERUN_LIMIT=2, immutable ledger decisions and deadline decisions. packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-wait.ts:22 defines the current six-outcome union, :24 the result, :35 the strict-green readiness function, :45 the runner/clock/sleep/scheduler seam, :67 the Poll union, :81 GH_FAILED including cancel, :102 GhCheck, :107 ghChecks, :124 classifyGh, :199 githubWaiting, :219 checksArgv, :225 pollOnce, :303 bindToHead, :312 terminalPoll, :330 errorRun, :362 checkHistory and :390 waitForChecks. The wait currently immediately returns failed only once pending checks settle. Preserve that ordering: only a would-be terminal GitHub failure gets job classification; mixed failed/pending timeout and error-history behavior must not acquire job reads. Extend parsed checks with state/link and carry ghChecks on failed/waiting polls. Call decideStarved at one site and starvedAtDeadline at one site, leaving loop complexity below the ratchet. Count rounds per wait, not per job, copy ledger sets rather than mutating EMPTY_STARVED_LEDGER, and distinguish old cancelled job ids from fresh rerun attempts. An old cancelled id already rerun must be ignored for job reads and round spending while other real failures still win. Only checks rerun by this wait can become starved at deadline; IN_PROGRESS work must remain pending. Do not accidentally use ledger names alone to waive a newly unrelated check or let a green/empty poll satisfy a vacuous deadline predicate.

Head binding is essential: githubWaiting currently only reads green/waiting polls (ci-wait.ts:199); ghHeadSha already supplies a fail-open headRefOid-only auxiliary read at :445. A would-be failed GitHub poll with expectedSha must read the head before any job read or POST; mismatch ends unavailable immediately with the existing sha8 wording. packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-wait.ts:414 currently reconstructs results as {outcome, detail}; change the return plumbing so starvedChecks survives both classification and deadline returns, while other outcomes omit it. Progress logging already uses workflow stage and storyId _run, and the wait's finally cancels heartbeat scheduling; preserve both on every new return path. New info/warn rerun lines should also be safe with no logger. packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-wait.ts:468 readChecksOnce and :492 verdictForHead are explicitly separate; they keep today's classifications and head-binding behavior even though shared checks argv adds link. No GitLab job I/O is introduced.

outOfScope: GitLab: a cancelled GitLab job or pipeline is never classed as starved and is never re-run.
`readChecksOnce` (the one-shot read behind `nax bot fix`'s gate baseline) keeps its current outcomes; a starved check there still reads as `failed`.
A check still queued at the deadline that this wait never re-ran stays `pending`, as today.
A failed check seen while other checks are still pending, at the deadline or at the error-poll limit, keeps today's `failed` outcome without a job read.
`nax workflow promote` never re-runs a job; only the run's publish and `nax bot fix` do.
The run's own publish never waives: a starved CI keeps the draft until a human runs `nax bot fix --waive-starved` or `nax workflow promote --waive-starved`.
Re-running a starved job outside a CI wait, as a command of its own.
`nax workflow status` shows a waiver only on a live read; a status that falls back to the run record (for example a PR with no item index) does not show it.
`latestCiWaiver` reads only comments by the current forge login, as the item index does; a waiver posted by another account is not shown.
A check name containing a backtick does not round-trip through the waiver record: the backtick is written as `'`.
Updating the nax-finish skill (repository `nax-toolkit-skills`) to offer `--waive-starved` is a manual follow-up outside this run.
A config key for the re-run limit: `CI_STARVED_RERUN_LIMIT` is a constant, as `CI_ERROR_POLL_LIMIT` is.
